notes.title: Tonal Contrasts in the Malipo Variety of the Mienic Language
notes.bp: A speech system should describe and recognize a language variety without erasing the contrast that makes the variety meaningful.
notes.wh: Small phonetic inventories and limited documentation make variation easy to mistake for noise or a universal norm.
notes.naive: Collapse the variety into a standard-language model and report only pooled accuracy.
notes.ap: Measure tonal contrasts in the Malipo variety as an object of speech description and evaluation.
notes.mech: Contrastive measurements expose which acoustic distinctions carry linguistic information.
notes.math: The paper treats dialect-and-variety as a structured evidence-to-decision problem: Contrastive measurements expose which acoustic distinctions carry linguistic information.
notes.eval: The paper reports an empirical study of tonal contrasts in a Mienic variety.
notes.ww: The paper reports an empirical study of tonal contrasts in a Mienic variety.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more population- or task-specific account of dialect-and-variety; the measured benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Speaker sample, elicitation design, tonal context, and language-specific scope bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners
notes.bp: Speech enhancement should improve access for a particular hearing-impaired listener, not merely optimize an average signal metric.
notes.wh: Hearing loss profiles differ, and a global enhancer can preserve the wrong cues.
notes.naive: Optimize one pooled enhancement objective and assume its score represents every listener.
notes.ap: Individualize enhancement around the listener's hearing profile and evaluate the resulting speech access.
notes.mech: Listener-specific constraints become the target of enhancement rather than the average waveform.
notes.math: The paper treats accessibility-fit as a structured evidence-to-decision problem: Listener-specific constraints become the target of enhancement rather than the average waveform.
notes.eval: The paper reports individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners.
notes.ww: The paper reports individualized speech enhancement for hearing-impaired listeners.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more population- or task-specific account of accessibility-fit; the measured benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Hearing profiles, listener numbers, fitting procedure, materials, and subjective protocol bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.

notes.title: Improving Child Speech Recognition and Reading Mistake Detection by Using Prompts
notes.bp: Child speech recognition and reading-mistake detection should connect variable child acoustics to intended linguistic units and learning outcomes.
notes.wh: Children differ in articulation, age, reading skill, and pronunciation, so adult-trained acoustic boundaries are unreliable.
notes.naive: Apply an adult ASR model and treat every mismatch as an ordinary recognition error.
notes.ap: Use prompts to condition recognition and mistake detection on the child's intended reading task.
notes.mech: Prompt information narrows the hypothesis space: acoustic evidence is interpreted with task and expected linguistic content.
notes.math: The paper treats pronunciation-variation as a structured evidence-to-decision problem: Prompt information narrows the hypothesis space: acoustic evidence is interpreted with task and expected linguistic content.
notes.eval: The paper reports improving child speech recognition and reading-mistake detection using prompts.
notes.ww: The paper reports improving child speech recognition and reading-mistake detection using prompts.
notes.po: The paper's payoff is a more population- or task-specific account of pronunciation-variation; the measured benefit remains author-reported.
notes.limits: Child age, language, prompt design, annotation policy, and error definitions bound transfer.
notes.evidence_boundary: D3 structured analyst note backed by captured PDF/text; result remains author-reported and was not independently reproduced.
